raw_response: {"diagnosis": "Batch 14 (362 rows) has source_tz='UTC', while every other batch is America/Chicago local time. Its txn_ts values are therefore UTC, which is 6 hours ahead of Chicago in January. This pushed the evening transactions past midnight into 2026-01-19 and left 2026-01-18 short. Converting UTC rows to Chicago local time restores consistent dates.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.88, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(ts_local AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(CAST(ts_local AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM (SELECT *, CASE WHEN source_tz = 'UTC' THEN timezone('America/Chicago', timezone('UTC', CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP))) ELSE CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) END AS ts_local FROM raw_transactions) WHERE status = 'POSTED'"}}
